extracted.intended_audience: horror/dark-fantasy writers, Horror Writers Association members, and general readers interested in the Bram Stoker Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Describes what the Bram Stoker Award recognizes (the HWA's stated standard of 'superior achievement' in dark fantasy and horror), the award categories (with years of eligibility), and the nomination and voting procedures used by the Horror Writers Association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose: 'superior achievement' in dark fantasy and horror writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bram Stoker Award is a recognition presented annually by the Horror Writers Association (HWA) for "superior achievement" in dark fantasy and horror writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The awards are explicitly issued "not based on 'best of the year' criteria, but 'for superior achievement'", a formulation that allows for ties. The HWA sought to avoid mean-spirited competition and to specifically seek out new and neglected writers and works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination sources: member recommendations and Jury lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominated works come from two different processes. Works can be recommended by any member of the HWA and a separate list of works is presented by a Jury for each category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both member recommendations and Jury selections feed into the preliminary ballot process (see voting process below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting process: preliminary and final ballots by Active members
rubrics_metrics.description: Members with Active status then vote on works appearing on preliminary ballots. The field is thereby narrowed to the Final ballot; and Active members vote to choose the winners from that Final Ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only Active members participate in the ballot stages (preliminary narrowing and final winner selection). The Jury's separate list is combined with member recommendations to determine what appears on ballots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and category structure (current categories as of 2021 eligibility year)
rubrics_metrics.description: As of the 2021 year of eligibility (ceremony convened in 2022), the Bram Stoker Award is presented for 'Superior Achievement' in the following categories: Novel (1987–), First Novel (1987–), Young Adult Novel (2011–), Middle Grade Novel (2022–), Graphic Novel (2011–), Long Fiction (1998–), Short Fiction (1998–), Anthology (1998–), Fiction Collection (1998–), Poetry Collection (2000–), Non-Fiction (1987–), Short Non-Fiction (2019–), Screenplay (1998–2004, 2011–), Lifetime Achievement (1987–).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category definitions and years of operation define the format/genre in which works are evaluated. The page also lists discontinued categories (e.g., Novelette 1987–1997; Short Story 1987–1997; Collection 1987–1997; Work for Young Readers 1998–2004; Alternative Forms/Other Media; Illustrated Narrative), which reflect historical changes in how works were classified and judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy of judging: encourage inclusivity and avoid competitive 'best of year' framing
rubrics_metrics.description: The HWA agreed to specifically seek out new and neglected writers and works, and officially issue Awards not based on 'best of the year' criteria, but 'for superior achievement', which allows for ties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guiding philosophy shapes nomination and selection practice (e.g., openness to lesser-known authors, allowance of ties) and signals that the awards emphasize recognized achievement rather than a strict single 'winner' ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ties are permitted under the award standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the awards are issued 'for superior achievement' rather than 'best of the year', ties are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowance of ties is an explicit feature of the award's standard and governance; it follows from the HWA's choice of 'superior achievement' as the evaluative phrase rather than a singular 'best'.
